content: 1. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as emtricitabine, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. It is recommended to avoid ARTs for at least one month prior to cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for the elimination of these medications. 2. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as enfuvirtide, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should not be taken for at least one month before cell mobilization or until the medications are fully eliminated. 3. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as etravirine, may disrupt the production of atidarsagene autotemcel. Avoid ARTs for at least one month prior to cell mobilization or for the duration necessary for their elimination. 4. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as fosamprenavir, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should not be used for at least one month before cell mobilization or until the medications are cleared. 5. The safety and effectiveness of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment have not been studied. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks preceding the start of myeloablative conditioning and until hematologic recovery is achieved. If feasible, childhood vaccinations should be administered before myeloablative conditioning. 6. The safety and effectiveness of the inactivated hepatitis A vaccine during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment have not been studied. Vaccination is not advised during the six weeks prior to myeloablative conditioning and until hematologic recovery is complete. Childhood vaccinations should be given before myeloablative conditioning if possible. 7. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks leading up to myeloablative conditioning and until hematologic recovery is achieved. Administer childhood vaccinations prior to myeloablative conditioning if feasible. 8.
